source_text: Nunc vero assero consequenter nihil Apostolum de Manichaea traduce suspicatum; ostendit quippe ad gravem iniuriam pertinere mysteriorum, si compararentur per cuncta peccatis, id est si non efficacius prodesset gratia, quam culpae forma nocuisset. Maximam ergo christianae fidei dignitatem in eo Magister Gentium collocavit, quod eam affirmavit antestare delictis; ob hoc illi curae fuit, ut morbis veteribus medicinae praeferret effectum.
pass_a_gloss: But now I assert consequently that the Apostle suspected nothing about the Manichaean tradux; for he showed that it belongs to a grave injury of the mysteries, if they were compared through all things to sins, that is if grace did not profit more effectively than the form of fault had harmed. The Teacher of the Gentiles therefore placed the greatest dignity of the Christian faith in this, that he affirmed that it stands before offenses; on this account it was a care to him that he prefer the effect of medicines to old diseases.

lemmas.lexica: LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: Now, however, I maintain consistently that the apostle had no notion of Manichaean inherited transmission. He showed that it would gravely insult the mysteries if they were in every respect comparable to sins—that is, if grace did not help more effectively than the example of sin had harmed. The Teacher of the Gentiles therefore located the Christian faith’s highest dignity in his affirmation that it surpasses offenses. That is why he took care to rank the medicine’s effect above the old diseases (compare Romans 5:15).

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)
